newsitem.title: JAPAN: Seoul says food crisis may force N.Korean collapse.
newsitem.headline: Seoul says food crisis may force N.Korean collapse.

text.p: The food crisis in North Korea could trigger a collapse in the communist government as it loses control over its hungry population, a South Korean official said on Tuesday.

With food supplies running out, North Korea was suffering a breakdown in its rationing system and its citizens were travelling freely across the country in search of food, South Korean ambassador-at-large Kim Ki-hwan said.
"The North Korean rationing system is breaking down," Kim told a news conference in Tokyo.
"North Korean authorities allow local governments to do whatever they can to find food and allow people to travel freely in search of food," he said.
"Under these circumstances, will it be possible for the regime to maintain tight control over its people?" he added.
Severe floods destroyed food stocks and grain harvests in North Korea in 1995 and 1996, pushing the Stalinist state onto the brink of famine.
International aid agencies have warned that tens of thousands of people could starve to death in North Korea over the next few months unless it receives substantial food aid.
"There is a high probability (of North Korea collapsing)," Kim said, although he did not say when the collapse could happen.
He said that, if the communist government fell apart, there would be a large-scale exodus of refugees to neighbouring countries such as South Korea, China and Japan.
Kim added that it was unlikely that North Korea would launch a military attack on rival South Korea because it could not secure support from any other countries.
Capitalist Seoul and communist Pyongyang have been technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean civil war, which ended in a truce.
Apart from acute shortages of food and fuel, North Korea's capabilities were undermined by military equipment that was obsolete and "rusted", he said.
North Korea said last week that the food crisis had reached a "serious stage" but that it would not go to war.
